findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded
findings.body: Each value in the appStore map is now a promise created when this module is evaluated (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). `import()` begins loading the target module immediately, so all 28 app packages are still fetched/parsed as soon as anything imports `@calcom/app-store` — the loading is not deferred to first use, which defeats the stated purpose of the PR. To get real lazy loading the values must be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites doing `await appStore[key]()`. Additionally, these module-scope promises float until a caller awaits them: if one of the dynamic imports ever rejects (failed/missing chunk) and that app key is never awaited, Node raises an unhandled promise rejection, which terminates the process by default on Node >= 15.

findings.title: requestReschedule: calendar deletions are now fire-and-forget behind an un-awaited dynamic import
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation the PR changed the booking-reference cleanup loop from a synchronous `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { const calendar = getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`. `forEach` does not await async callbacks and nothing else awaits them, and there is no surrounding try/catch. Before this change `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` was invoked synchronously, so the provider API calls were in flight before the mutation sent the reschedule email and returned; now each callback suspends at `await getCalendar(...)` (the dynamic import) and the deletion only starts later, possibly after the response has been sent — on serverless platforms the function can be frozen before `deleteEvent` ever runs, leaving stale events on the organizer's calendar. Failures inside the callback (import or deleteEvent rejection) become unhandled promise rejections instead of surfaced errors. Fix by awaiting the work: `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel path: awaiting getCalendar inside fire-and-forget forEach defers deleteEvent past the end of the request
findings.body: In the branch that cancels all remaining occurrences of a recurring event, the code does `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... await calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId); ... })`. The `await getCalendar(...)` added by this PR makes each callback suspend on the dynamic import before `deleteEvent` is ever invoked; previously `getCalendar` was synchronous, so every `deleteEvent` HTTP call was started synchronously while the forEach ran. Nothing awaits the forEach callbacks, and the pushes into `apiDeletes` happen only after those callbacks resume — i.e. after the handler already executed `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (which snapshots the array) and returned success. The net effect is that deleting the calendar events for all future occurrences of a cancelled recurring booking may never start before the request completes (and may never run at all on serverless), leaving cancelled occurrences on users' calendars. Collect the promises (e.g. with `map`) and include them in the final `Promise.all`.

findings.title: forEach made async: errors escape the surrounding try/catch and deletions are no longer started before returning
findings.body: The PR changed `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { const calendar = getCalendar(...); ... })` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`. Because `forEach` ignores the promises returned by async callbacks, (1) the `try/catch` wrapped around this loop no longer catches anything — a rejection from `getCalendar` (dynamic import) or from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` becomes an unhandled promise rejection (fatal by default on Node >= 15) instead of being logged by the catch block; and (2) `deleteEvent` is no longer invoked synchronously, so the function can send the reschedule email and return `true` before the calendar deletion has even started, which on serverless deployments means it may never run. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` so the work completes and errors remain observable.

findings.title: forEach made async: errors escape the surrounding try/catch and deletions are no longer started before returning
findings.body: The PR changed `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { const calendar = getCalendar(...); ... })` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`. Because `forEach` ignores the promises returned by async callbacks, (1) the `try/catch` wrapped around this loop no longer catches anything — a rejection from `getCalendar` (dynamic import) or from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` becomes an unhandled promise rejection (fatal by default on Node >= 15) instead of being logged by the catch block; and (2) `deleteEvent` is no longer invoked synchronously, so the function can send the reschedule email and return `true` before the calendar deletion has even started, which on serverless deployments means it may never run. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` so the work completes and errors remain observable.
